posts.title: The Ultimate Guide to Choosing the Best Medical College in 2024
posts.content:
Choosing the right medical college after completing your 12th class in the medical stream can be a difficult task given the vast number of options available both nationally and internationally. It is crucial to exercise patience and diligence in selecting the best college, as it will shape your future career prospects. Your college education will enable you to build on your foundational knowledge and develop essential skills for your chosen profession.

To identify the ideal medical college for admission, there are several key factors to consider :

Total expenses: Choosing the best college to study MBBS abroad requires you to consider your budget first. Some colleges offer the complete course expenses, including food and hostel, at a low cost, while others can charge you more than 25-30 lakh for the same facilities.

Mode of teaching: To avoid language barriers and gain a clear understanding of the subject, it is important for students to ensure that the medium of instruction for the MBBS program they are considering abroad is English before taking admission.

Recognition: It is crucial to keep in mind that pursuing an MBBS degree from an international institution is only considered valid in India if the institution is recognized and approved by the National Medical Commission. This is especially important for students who plan to practice medicine in India after completing their degree.

Location of the university: Although it may not be crucial in terms of the quality of education, the location of the MBBS abroad college is still an important factor to consider. This is one reason why countries like the Philippines, Russia, Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan are becoming popular choices for MBBS studies abroad, as they offer favorable living conditions and amenities

Duration of courses: Compared to India, different countries have varying education systems that offer flexibility in the course duration. For example, medical universities in Russia, China, and Ukraine have a 6-year course duration. While, in Georgia, medical universities have both 5 and 6 years courses.. In Kyrgyzstan, some universities provide a 5-year course duration. It’s important for students to understand that saving a year in their education is significant, and course duration is a crucial factor to consider when choosing a medical college abroad.

posts.title: MD in Obstetrics and Gynaecology : Admission, Eligibility, Fees and Top Colleges
posts.content:
MD in Obstetrics and Gynaecology is a full-time postgraduate medical course that spans three years. It combines two medical specialities that deal with female reproductive organs, namely obstetrics (during pregnancy) and gynaecology (outside of pregnancy). These two specialities are often combined to create a single medical discipline and postgraduate training program.

The MD Obstetrics & Gynecology course focuses on various topics such as Obstetrics Pathology, Gynecological Obstetrics and Gynecology, and common diseases related to pregnancy. It also covers neonatal hygiene, infant care, and breastfeeding. The course equips students with the necessary skills to manage complicated pregnancies, perform obstetric operations, and handle common disorders related to newborn babies. After completing this course, individuals can pursue a rewarding career in the field of Obstetrics & Gynecology.

In India, there are a total of 404 colleges/hospitals offering the MD Obstetrics and Gynaecology course, with a total of 3552 seats available. The number of seats available for MD in Obstetrics and Gynaecology is not easily available as it is a different course.

MD in Obstetrics and Gynaecology Eligibility

  • The recognition cut-off dates for the medical college’s MBBS Degree courses and compulsory rotatory internship must be as prescribed by the MCI.
  • Candidates required to have completed a one-year compulsory rotating internship in a teaching institution or other institution recognized by the MCI.
  • Candidates must have obtained permanent registration with any State Medical Council.

Meeting these eligibility requirements is necessary to apply for and be considered for admission to an MD in Obstetrics and Gynecology program.

posts.title: MD in Radiology : Admission, Eligibility, Fees and Top Colleges
posts.content:
MD in Radiology is a postgraduate medical program with a duration of three years. This course focuses on the science of radiology, which involves the use of X-rays and other high-energy radiation to identify medical issues and determine the appropriate treatment. A radiologist, who is also a physician, uses radio technology to diagnose medical conditions and provide treatment options.

The program provides in-depth knowledge on various aspects of radiology, such as the production of X-rays, radio physics, interaction of radio with the matter, radiography, special radiography, radiation detection and measurement, among others.

MD in Radiology : Overview

Course NameDoctor of Medicine in Radiology
Course LevelPostgraduate
Duration3 years
EligibilityM.B.B.S + Internship
Entrance ExamNEET - PG
Average Course FeeINR 40,000 Per Annum to 8 Lakhs Per Annum

Why Pursue MD in Radiology?

  • Many people choose to pursue radiology as a profession because they find the diagnostic challenges interesting.
  • Radiology offers numerous opportunities for professional development.
  • The field of radiology provides knowledge on radiography, radiation protection, image formation, radio diagnosis, CT scan, MRI, and Mammography, among others.
  • Pursuing a postgraduate degree in radiology can also be a suitable path for those interested in pursuing a PhD since it provides ample knowledge about the field.

MD in Radiology Eligibility

  • Students must then complete a 5-year MBBS degree or a similar degree in medical science, with at least 55% aggregate.
  • They must also complete a 1-year in-house internship during their MBBS course.
  • Candidates need to pass the NEET-PG or other designated entrance exams with the required marks.

MD in Radiology Admission Process

posts.title: MD in Dermatology, Leprosy, and Venereology: Admission, Eligibility Criteria, and Fees
posts.content:
The Doctor of Medicine in Dermatology, Venereology & Leprosy, also known as M.D. (Dermatology, Venereology & Leprosy), is a three-year postgraduate program that students can pursue after completing MBBS. This program deals with the study of skin, nails, hair, and related diseases. The National Medical Commission (NMC) has released guidelines for a competency-based postgraduate training program for MDs in Dermatology, Venereology & Leprosy.

This program aims to create specialists who can provide high-quality health care and contribute to advances in science through research and training. The program includes required training that helps students recognize the health needs of the community, handle medical problems effectively, and stay aware of recent advances in their specialty. The candidate should possess a broad range of skills that enable them to practice independently, teach medical/para-medical students, and understand research methodology.

In India, there are 106 government colleges that offer MD Dermatology courses. The total number of MD Dermatology seats in government colleges across different states of the country is 455. Among all states, Tamil Nadu has the highest number of MD Dermatology seats with 44 available.

Course Overview

Name of Course MD in Dermatology, Leprosy, and Venereology
Level Postgraduate
Duration of Course 3 Years
Minimum Academic Requirement MBBS degree obtained from any college/university recognized by the Medical Council of India
Admission Process Entrance Exam (NEET PG)

Counselling by DGHS/MCC/State Authorities

INI CET for various AIIMS, PGIMER Chandigarh, JIPMER Puducherry, NIMHANS Bengaluru
Course fees Rs. 40K to 10 Lakh per annum
Average Salary Rs. 5 Lakh to 15 Lakh per annum

Primary Objective of  Course

  • Diagnose and manage common skin diseases, sexually transmitted diseases, and leprosy.
  • Effectively manage medical emergencies related to skin, leprosy, and venereal disease.
  • Implement preventative measures against communicable, venereal diseases, and leprosy at both individual and community levels.
  • Teach necessary knowledge and laboratory skills to medical and paramedical team members.
  • Maintain a compassionate attitude towards patients and their families.
  • Evaluate and initiate investigations to solve problems related to skin, venereal diseases, and leprosy.

  • The recognition cut-off dates for the medical college’s MBBS Degree courses and compulsory rotatory internship must be as prescribed by the Medical Council of India (now NMC).
  • Candidates are required to have completed a one-year compulsory rotating internship in a teaching institution or other institution recognized by the MCI.
  • The candidate must have obtained permanent registration with any State Medical Council.

MD Dermatology  Admission Process

posts.title: Postgraduate Specializations after MBBS
posts.content:
As a candidate for the medical school exam, you face tough competition. But have you thought about your career options after completing your MBBS degree? Relying solely on your MBBS degree may not be enough to establish a successful practice or secure a position in a top hospital or research facility. To advance your career, you should consider pursuing postgraduate specializations offered by India’s top medical institutes. These specializations can help you stand out and excel in your field.

Why PG specialisation is important after MBBS?

Improve career prospects : After pursuing MBBS it is very important for the students to carry on studies to get specialization in a particular field. it will help to boost their career and will open the door to many opportunities.

Got your promotion and raise : When you are working somewhere without any specialization, then the higher authority doesn’t bother you. The management is always keen to draw maximum benefits from special skills that students will pursue after MBBS .so it is very important for students to pursue pg after MBBS.

Personality development : Pursuing a postgraduate Specializations degree can broaden your horizons and enhance your personal development. With exposure to a wider range of perspectives, you are better equipped to envision the bigger picture and develop more sophisticated solutions.

More financially stable : Having a postgraduate degree can significantly enhance your earning potential in the job market compared to having just a bachelor’s degree. Employers are likely to recognize the added value and depth of knowledge that comes with advanced education and may offer you more lucrative compensation packages.

PG Medical Entrance Exam :

Two types of the medical entrance after MBBS

National Eligibility Entrance Test for Post Graduate (NEET-PG):

To appear for NEET PG, the entrance exam for admission to postgraduate medical courses in India, you must:

  • Have completed MBBS from an MCI-recognized college.
  • no upper age limit.
  • Have completed one year of internship before the exam.

The exam pattern for NEET PG is as follows:

  • It is a computer-based test (CBT) with 200 multiple-choice questions (MCQs).
  • The duration of the exam is 3 hours.
  • The syllabus includes all 19 subjects studied during the MBBS course.
  • Each correct answer is worth 4 marks, while each wrong answer will result in one mark being deducted.

Institute of National Importance Combined Entrance Test (INI CET) :

To be eligible for INI-CET, the national-level entrance exam for admission to postgraduate Specializations medical courses in India, you must:

  • Have completed MBBS from an MCI-recognized institute.

The exam pattern for INI-CET is as follows:

  • It is a computer-based test (CBT) with 200 multiple-choice questions (MCQs).
  • The syllabus covers topics from all subjects taught during the MBBS course.
  • The exam duration is 3 hours.
  • There are four sections – A (Basic Sciences), B (Clinical Sciences), C (Preclinical Sciences), and D (Paraclinical Sciences).

posts.title: NEET UG 2023: Study MBBS in Russia-Eligibility, Fees and Colleges
posts.content:
Study MBBS in Russia has now become the prime alternative of students seeking MBBS in abroad as russia remained a top study-abroad destination for Indian medical students, with a reported 18,039 Indian students studying in the country in the year 2022. Although the Indian Ministry of External Affairs does not specifically track the courses of study pursued by these students, data from the National Board of Examinations (NBE) indicates that in 2021, 4,515 Indian students sat for the Foreign Medical Graduate Examination (FMGE) and 1,119 of them successfully passed the screening test.

Eligibility to study MBBS in Russia

  • Must have obtained at least a 50% aggregate score in Physics, Chemistry, and Biology (PCB) subjects in their Class 12 board examination.
  • Should have qualified for the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET) with a minimum score that places them in the 50th percentile or above.
  • Must have a medical clearance certifying that they are free from any contagious diseases.
  • The minimum age requirement is 17 years.

Course Structure

  • In Russia, an MBBS degree is a six-year program, with five years dedicated to academic study and one year for an internship.
  • Dentistry and pharmacy courses last for five years, and nursing courses last for four years.
  • The first three years focus on the theoretical part, while the latter three years focus on practical training.
  • There are 12 semesters in total, with each year divided into two semesters.
  • After completing four years, students receive a bachelor’s degree and a diploma in higher education.
  • Students can continue their studies and pursue a Master’s program.
  • The academic session typically begins between September and October in Russia.

The Admission Process to Study MBBS in Russia

  • Admission to MBBS courses in Russia does not require an entrance exam.
  • Interested students must visit the website of the university/institute they wish to apply to and fill out the corresponding application form.
  • Students are required to submit all necessary documents, such as proof of identity and educational qualifications.
  • University authorities will verify the submitted information and will contact selected students via email.

MBBS Fees in Russia

  • The MBBS fees in Russia for Indian students are lower compared to other countries like the US, UK.
  • The full-time MBBS degree program typically costs can range between 5000 USD to 6000 USD per academic year.
  • Other daily expenses, such as food, transportation and study materials should also be taken into account when budgeting for the study mbbs in Russia.

Best Colleges to Study MBBS in Russia

posts.title: How to Choose  PG specialization after MBBS?
posts.content:
Choosing a postgraduate ( PG ) specialization after MBBS can be a daunting decision, but here are some factors to consider that might help you to choose the perfect course for you.

  • Personal interests and career goals:  consider what area of medicine you find interesting and enjoyable to study. Just focus and think about long-term goals and which specialities will take you high in your career. 
  • Job prospect: look into the course which has high demand in your country or region. And always choose the course in which you have high interest. and it is fine to change your career path when you realize you are not passionate about it. your interest is the first priority.
  • Availability of training programs: check the availability of the programs for the specializations in which you have a high level of interest.  
  • Work-life balance: it is very important for the aspirants to choose the specialties in which they can maintain the work-life balance. Some specialities demand long hours and on-call duties, while some offer more flexible work schedules. 
  • Salary and compensation:  why do students prefer medical education ? one reason is highly reputed and the other one is it rewards high salary and compensation. so look into the salary and compensation packages for different specialities. Always keep in mind that some specialities may be more financially rewarding than others.
  • Professional development opportunities: Different specialities offer different opportunities. opportunities related to research, teaching and leadership roles.
  •  Evaluate your strengths and weaknesses: understanding your strengths and weaknesses can help in choosing the best specializations after MBBS. Consider the specializations which you explore during the MBBS course. 
  • Go for the most reputed college:  The reputation of the institution where you pursue your postgraduate specialization can also play an important role in your future career prospects. Go for the institution which has a good track of producing successful doctors in your chosen field.

Some Best PG Course after MBBS

 

  •  MD/MS in clinical medicine: it refers to the specialization of the diagnosis, treatment and prevention of diseases and involves a combination of clinical practice and research. 
  • MD/MS in Surgery: it refers to surgical procedures both major and minor, and also includes the combination of practical and research.  
  • MD in Pediatrics: it refers to a focus on the medical care of infants, children and adolescents and also includes treatment and diagnosis. 
  • MD in Obstetrics and Gynecology: it refers to the medical and surgical care of women during pregnancy, childbirth, and postpartum, and includes diagnosis and treatment of gynaecological disorders.
  • MD in Radiology: it refers to the use of imaging technology to diagnose and treat diseases, including X-rays, CT scans, MRIs, and ultrasounds.
  • MD in Anesthesiology: it refers to the administration of anesthesia to patients undergoing surgical procedures and other medical treatments.

Ultimately, the choice of PG specialization will depend on your personal interests, career goals, and the specific opportunities available to you. It may also be helpful to speak with practicing doctors in different specialities and attend medical conferences or seminars to gain a better understanding of the various fields.

posts.title: Last Minute Preparation  Tips and Strategies  for NEET PG 2023
posts.content:
NEET PG 2023 is one of the most competitive medical entrance exams in India, and with the exam approaching fast, it’s essential to make the most of your preparation time. Here are some last-minute tips to help you prepare for the exam.

Revise thoroughly: At this point, it’s important to revise all the topics you’ve covered during your NEET PG 2023 preparation. Go through your notes and revise the concepts, formulas, and theories.

Practice with mock tests: Take as many mock tests as you can. This will help you get familiar with the exam pattern, manage your time better, and identify your weak areas.

Go through the previous question paper:  Refer to the previous year’s question papers to get an idea of the exam pattern and difficulty level. Additionally, many coaching institutes and publishers offer previous question papers and study material for NEET PG exam preparation. You can try practising these question papers to assess your preparation level and identify areas that need improvement.

Focus on your weak areas: Use your mock test results to identify your weak areas and focus on improving them. Spend more time on the topics that you find difficult and try to get a good grip on them.

Manage your time: Time management is crucial during the exam. Practice solving questions quickly and accurately. Divide your time for each section of the exam and stick to it.

Stay calm and positive: It’s natural to feel nervous before the exam, but try to stay calm and positive. Trust your preparation and believe in yourself. Do some relaxation exercises and meditation to help calm your nerves.

Eat well and sleep well: Eating well and getting enough sleep is important for your overall health and well-being. Make sure you eat a healthy, balanced diet, and get at least 7-8 hours of sleep each night.

Read the question carefully: Read the questions carefully before attempting to answer them. Don’t rush through the questions and make sure you understand what is being asked.

Use shortcuts: During the exam, you can use shortcuts to save time. For example, use the elimination method to rule out options that are obviously incorrect.

Don’t get stuck: If you come across a question that you find difficult, don’t get stuck on it. Move on to the next question and come back to it later if you have time.

Stay updated with current affairs: Stay updated with current affairs related to science and technology, medical breakthroughs, and healthcare-related news. This will help you answer questions related to these topics.

 

In conclusion, preparing for NEET PG 2023 requires dedication, hard work, and smart strategies. Remember to stay focused, stay positive, and believe in yourself. Preparing for NEET PG 2023 requires a disciplined approach and consistent effort. With the exam approaching fast, it’s important to make the most of your preparation time. By revising thoroughly, practicing with mock tests, focusing on your weak areas, managing your time, staying calm and positive, eating well and sleeping well, reading the questions carefully, using shortcuts, not getting stuck, and staying updated with current affairs, you can give your best shot at the exam.

Currently, the eligibility criteria for NEET UG 2023 have not been released. To be eligible for NEET UG 2023, candidates must have passed the 10+2 or an equivalent level exam with Physics, Chemistry, Biology/Bio-technology, and English as subjects. According to the NEET UG 2022 Information Bulletin, the test pattern of NEET (UG) – 2022 included four subjects, each consisting of two sections. posts.title: HOW TO PREPARE FOR THE NEET PG?
posts.content:
NEET-PG is a qualifying and ranking examination held by the National Board of Examinations (NBE) for aspirants wishing to pursue postgraduate Doctor of Medicine (MD), Master of Surgery (MS), and diploma courses in India’s government and private medical colleges. It is a computer-based examination consisting of 200 multiple-choice questions that candidates must answer in two hours and thirty minutes. According to the marking scheme, the candidate receives four points for each correct answer, and one point is deducted for each incorrect answer.

 

Given the examination’s difficulty and competitiveness, now is the ideal time for all candidates to begin their preparation.

 

  1. Regular study: All aspirants must ensure that they can devote at least six to eight hours of their day to their studies. They must divide their daily preparation into four one-and-a-half to two-hour study sessions. This will help to reduce the extra burden while also ensuring that the candidates’ attention span is not compromised. Taking regular breaks between sessions allows aspirants to relax and prepare more effectively.

 

  1. Focus on key topics: Aspirants should concentrate on topics such as Medicine, Surgery, Obstetrics and Gynecology, Preventive and Social Medicine, Pathology, Pharma, and Microbiology during their preparations because these subjects account for approximately 70 to 75% of the questions in the examination.

 

 

  1. Strategic Revision: Aspirants should devote at least one to two hours per day to revising key topics and weak areas to strengthen their concepts. To improve preparation efficiency, aspirants should use a single source of revision for each subject to add all important pointers and notes. Online platforms can assist aspirants in clarifying concepts and providing a brief and concise explanation of the same.

 

  1. Practise papers and mock tests: Because NEET PG is one of the most competitive exams, aspirants frequently experience anxiety and tenseness as the exam approaches. To help alleviate this anxiety, candidates must complete multiple practice tests and answer approximately 100 MCQs per day.

 

They must also concentrate on answering question papers from previous editions of the exam. This will allow them to gain a better understanding of the pattern and topics that will be covered in the exam, allowing them to feel more confident about their preparation.

 

  1. Prioritized Self-Care: Throughout their preparation, all aspirants must prioritize self-care. It is critical to stay healthy to effectively prepare for the exam. Aspirants should not jeopardize their mental or physical health. Exam-related discussions, for example, must take place in groups of no more than three to five people. Late-night studies frequently disrupt aspirants’ sleep schedules and should thus be avoided. Prioritizing self-care boosts motivation and confidence, making it an essential component of any aspirant’s preparation strategy.

 

For more counseling and advice on cracking your NEET PG examination, the A R Group Of Education is here to help you out. We are equipped with highly trained professionals who can guide you through every step. From exam preparation to MBBS Admissions, we have a team of experienced and skilled preceptors who will train you and stand with you in your journey.

posts.title: EVERYTHING YOU SHOULD KNOW ABOUT NEET PG COUNSELING?
posts.content:
NEET PG is a ranking-based admission exam for MD/MS and PG diploma programs. It is a single-window admissions exam for postgraduate courses offered by the government, private, and deemed universities throughout the country. Every year, a large number of candidates take the national entrance exam. It is managed by the National Board of Education.

 

The Medical Counselling Committee (MCC) has declared the dates for students who have passed the National Eligibility Cumulative Entrance Test-Postgraduate (NEET-PG) exams to be counseled. On August 20th, the counseling process will begin. NEET PG Counselling 2021 is a statewide counseling effort that includes all states, territories, and universities. Counseling for all India 50% quota seats is organized by the MCC on an all-India basis. Admission will be granted only after all eligibility requirements have been met, following which counseling will be offered.

 

Round 1 of NEET PG Counselling 2023

 

Following the release of the NEET PG 2023 seat allotment for counseling round one, candidates must take the steps outlined below based on their status. If an applicant fails to report to the identified institute within the specified time frame, the seat allotted in the initial round of MCC NEET PG counseling will be deleted. This is referred to as a “free exit.”

Accepting the seat allotted in the first round of NEET PG 2023 counseling: If a candidate is delighted with the seat assigned in the first round of NEET PG 2023 counseling, they can report to the assigned institute and secure their place by offering to pay the education money.

 

Round 2 of NEET PG Counselling 2023

 

Candidates in the NEET PG Counselling 2023 Round 2 must meet the following eligibility criteria:

  • Candidates who were not offered a seat in the first round of NEET PG counseling in 2023.
  • Candidates who received seats in the first round of NEET PG admission were denied during physical document verification.
  • Candidates who wish to advance to the second round of NEET PG 2023 counseling.
  • Candidates who chose a free exit or did not attend NEET PG round one counseling

 

NEET PG Counselling Mop Round 2023

  • The MCC NEET PG mop-up round will only be held for admission to deemed, central, and ESIC colleges.
  • Candidates who did not report to their assigned college in round one or round two of NEET PG 2023 counseling will be required to reapply for the mop-up round.
  • Candidates who did not receive a seat in round one or round two of NEET PG counseling will not be required to reapply for the mop-up round. All candidates will have to change their courses and colleges.
  • The official website will announce the mop-up round seat allotment for NEET PG 2023.

 

NEET PG Counselling Seats 2023 State Quota

 

For the surviving 50% state quota seats and 100% seats in private institutes, NEET PG 2023 counselling will be initiated by respective state agencies. After the NBE makes an announcement about the NEET PG result 2023, the state quota counselling process will begin. State quota NEET PG counselling would fill 50% of seats in government colleges and 100% of seats in private colleges in the state. Each state will provide an application form for NEET PG 2023 state admission counselling.

 

Candidates must meet the necessary eligibility criteria, which include a minimum NEET PG cut-off, educational qualifications, domicile, and other factors, in order to participate in state NEET PG counselling 2023. The counselling authority will release the NEET PG state merit list of eligible candidates. Candidates will be expected to fill out their preferences for colleges and coursework, as well as provide necessary documents, during NEET PG counselling for state quota seats. Based on their preferences, NEET PG 2023 state rank, booking requirements, and other variables, candidates will be allotted MD, MS, and PG diploma seats in the state.

 

Seat Allocation for NEET PG Counselling in 2023

 

When the registration process for round one of NEET PG counseling is completed, the DGHS will handle seat allocation. MCC will allocate the NEET PG 2021 seat allotment messages for shortlisted candidates on the official website. NEET PG seat allocation for 2021 will be determined by NEET PG rank, college and course preferences, available seats, reservation criteria, and other factors. Based on these considerations, the NEET PG 2021 counseling outcome will be announced on the MCC website following seat allotment processing. The PDF of the NEET PG seat allocation result for 2021 will be made available. It will include information about the candidate, such as rank, institute, and course.

 

NEET PG Counselling 2023 Documents

The following NEET PG 2023 documents are required:

  • NEET PG admit card – revised date
  • Result
  • Admit card – revised date
  • Result Mark Sheets of MBBS/BDS professional examinations
  • MBBS/BDS Degree Certificate
  • Internship Completion Certificate
  • MCI issued a registration certificate
  • Date of birth
  • proof Valid ID proof (Aadhar; Passport; Voter’s ID; Pan Card; Driver’s License) (if applicable)

 

Please contact the A R Group Of Education for more information and guidance on the subject. We have highly qualified professionals to help you with every detail about NEET PG and the application process.

 

The A R Group Of Education streamlines the application process for students aspiring to be doctors. The initial counselling sessions provided by in-house counsellors address all types of student concerns and questions, clearing the fog that has settled over their minds. Furthermore, our faculty will assist you in deciding which medical speciality you want to pursue in your studies in order to have a successful career in the medical field.

posts.title: Advantages Of Studying MBBS in Philippines
posts.content:
The Philippines is a sovereign state located in Southeast Asia’s western Pacific Ocean. It is a lovely country with beautiful beaches and a tropical climate. Manila is the country’s capital. The country has breathtaking natural beauty and a diverse mix of cultures and communities. Previously, the Philippines was ruled by Spain and America. Filipinos have a strong affinity for fast food, movies, and music.

 

The country with a rich mix of cultural context and breathtaking elegance attracts tourists from all over the world, but it also attracts students from 65 countries for the reasons listed below. There are many excellent universities in the Philippines.

 

The Philippines’ literacy rate

 

The Philippines has the highest literacy rate in Asia, at 94%! That means that the majority of people in the Philippines are educated and of a certain social class. That makes the country remarkable and safe for medical students to study in.

 

The Philippines is an English-speaking country, making it ideal for MBBS in Philippines!

 

English is an international language that is spoken as either the first or second language in the majority of countries around the world. It is also used as a second language in our country, following our native language Hindi, in accordance with international standards. The Philippines, the world’s third-largest economy, is not far behind.

 

The Philippines, the world’s third-largest English-speaking country, is not far behind. English is the medium of instruction at all levels of education, including MBBS in the Philippines. English is the medium of instruction at all levels of education, including MBBS in the Philippines.

 

Students are very safe in the Philippines

 

The Philippines is a female-dominated country, with females predominating in all workplaces and accounting for more than 60% of the population. It is appropriate for both boys and girls. The Philippines is a melting pot of cultures, which makes it a welcoming country, giving students an advantage in not being treated as outsiders or foreigners.

Students who study here feel more at ease in the welcoming environment of the country and are able to concentrate better on their studies.

 

After 10+2, the Philippines offers a DUAL Degree programme for MBBS

 

A dual degree programme is possible with the medicine study programme in the Philippines. Before receiving the degree of MD, students in the BS-MD programme earn a Bachelor of Science (BS) ( Doctor of medicine). BS programmes last between one and a half and two years, depending on the university.

 

Opportunities for advancement are provided by an MBBS from the Philippines

 

With many top universities, the Philippines has become a medical education hub. Students studying here would have a broader perspective. Students who study medicine in the Philippines after graduation have a better chance of finding work in other countries. This is an opportunity to study at a good university while also travelling and learning about a new country. There are also opportunities to travel around the world.

 

Climate

 

The Philippines is known as a Tropical Weather Country, with temperatures ranging from 24 to 34 degrees Celsius all year. It is very easy for Indian students to adjust to the weather there.

 

MBBS in the Philippines is Reasonably Priced

 

The Philippines is a very affordable destination. Low-cost lodging and living expenses. The course fees are significantly lower than in India. There is no donation system.

 

Excellent transportation and air connectivity

 

The Philippines is well connected to the rest of the world, with three international airports in Manila, Cebu, and Davao connecting to all major cities worldwide. Buses, taxis, metros, and other modes of public transportation are available in Manila, allowing students to easily travel throughout the Philippines. India has five countries that connect it to the Philippines by air.

 

Education in the United States

 

The Philippines has a PBL curriculum in the American style. The education system in the Philippines is based on that of the United States. It is simple to pass the USMLE. Many toppers from the Philippines go to the United States for the Residency Program.

 

Religion

 

The Philippines is a predominantly Christian country. Over 90% of the population is Christian. The Philippines is a friendly country because it is a melting pot of different cultures.

 

Indian Cuisine

 

South Indian and North Indian cuisine are both available in the Philippines. In the Philippines, there is no shortage of Indian cuisine. Some medical schools operate an Indian Mess on the university campus. There is also a private hostel with Indian cuisine.

posts.title: Let’s Know About Lyceum Northwestern University, Philippines
posts.content:
Lyceum Northwestern University in the Philippines has a more than 50-year history of offering top-notch MBBS education and academic achievement in South Asia.

 

Every year, students from all over the world come here to pursue their dreams in fields such as medicine, arts and sciences, business education, criminology, architecture, law, engineering, and other vocational studies. University’s MBBS Education is world-renowned for its comprehensive curriculum and research centers. There is a huge group of Indian students who study at the Lyceum Northwestern University campus to pursue their long-held dreams of becoming doctors.

 

The university is dedicated to developing compassionate, knowledgeable, and highly competent physicians by providing early hands-on clinical training and opportunities to hone professional skills. Moreover, they are also well-known for building a community of scholars and professionals dedicated to serving society, as well as assisting students in reaching their full potential as competent, ethical, caring, and inquiring citizens and visionary leaders.

 

Eligibility requirements for admission to the University:

Students in the General Category with a minimum of 50% in physics, chemistry, and biology are eligible to enroll.

Students from the SC and SEBC categories with a 40% aggregate in physics, chemistry, and biology are eligible to enroll in the AMA School of Medicine. In addition to the science marks, students must have a passing grade in English.

 

Weather conditions:

The Philippines has five climates: tropical rainforest, tropical savannah, tropical monsoon, humid subtropical, and oceanic (both in higher-altitude areas), all of which are characterized by relatively high temperatures, oppressive humidity, and abundant rainfall. Based on the amount of rainfall, the country has two seasons: a wet season and a dry season. This is also dependent on where you live in the country, as some areas get rain all year (see Climate types). The warmest months of the year are determined by temperature. The warmest months of the year are March through October, with the winter monsoon bringing cooler air from November to February. The warmest month is May, and the coolest is January.

 

Duration of the course:

For students who have completed class 12 with Science, the total duration of the Medical, MD, or MBBS course is 5 and a half years. The first 16 months are devoted to a pre-medical course. It focuses on laying the groundwork for a solid medical education. The next four years are dedicated to core medicine and clinical rotations.

 

The advantages of Lyceum North Western University are as follows:

  1. Admission does not require a donation.
  2. Admission does not require an entrance exam.
  3. Low college tuition
  4. Fully furnished hostel facility
  5. Canteens serving Gujarati and other Indian cuisines
  6. The library is open 24 hours a day, seven days a week for reading.
  7. cutting-edge technology in a campus hospital for best practices
  8. Wi-Fi is available around the clock.
  9. A secure environment and well-mannered people
  10. The University provides excellent boarding and lodging.

 

Practical Experience:

Medical Courses in the Philippines are generally Practical Oriented, following the pattern of the United States, where the LNU Medical Program is more practical-oriented and provides practical exposure to its medical students through an affiliation with government hospitals and medical centers. LNU students receive training at Region 1 Medical Centre and other Dagupan government hospitals.

Bachelor of Medicine and Bachelor of Surgery (MBBS) is one of India’s most prestigious courses. Candidates who complete an MBBS degree are eligible to become qualified doctors. Every year, millions of students dream to be doctors. However, only a few are admitted to MBBS programs in India. Obtaining an MBBS seat is a highly competitive process. Every year, over 18 lakh aspirants compete for a seat at India’s prestigious medical college. The first hurdle for candidates seeking MBBS admission is passing the NEET.

 

The NEET exam is given once a year by the National Testing Agency (NTA). According to the Supreme Court of India, NEET-UG is the single national-level entrance examination for MBBS admission in India. The NEET exam also grants admission to 1,899 MBBS seats at AIIMS institutions and 249 seats at JIPMER. Based on NEET scores, 612 medical colleges, 15 AIIMS, and 2 JIPMER institutions offer MBBS admission. When MBBS seats are compared to the number of aspirants who take the exam, the competition for MBBS admission in India is rising exponentially. Many students who score low on the NEET exam struggle to gain admission to government medical schools. Private MBBS colleges, on the other hand, charge exorbitant fees.

 

Due to the obvious high tuition fees in India, many students from the middle class struggle to gain admission to the MBBS programs. These students’ only hope is to qualify for MBBS admission in India if they pass the NEET exam. The NTA screening process for MBBS admission is very rigorous and entirely based on NEET exam merit. Following the announcement of the NEET result, the Medical Counselling Committee (MCC) oversees the MBBS admission process. MCC offers MBBS admission to 15% All India Quota, deemed/central universities, AFMC, and Employee State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) institutes. MBBS admission to the remaining 85% of state quota seats is bestowed with good grades by the respective state counselling authorities.

 

The NTA screening process for MBBS admission is very stringent and entirely based on NEET exam merit. posts.title: What you should know about MCC NEET PG Counseling?
posts.content:
The National Eligibility Cumulative Entrance Test Post Graduate, abbreviated as NEET PG, is India’s primary qualifying entrance and rank-determining exam. Every year, it is held by the National Board of Examinations, which is part of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India. It is the successor to the All India Post Graduate Medical Entrance Examination (AIPGMEE).

Guidelines:

If a student chooses to pursue the following courses, he or she must take the examination for the same.

  1. Master of Surgery (MS)
  2. Doctor Of Medicine (MD)
  3. Diploma courses from any government or private college in India.

 

 

NEET PG is a computer-based examination, and the subjects tested follow the Graduate Medical Education Regulations syllabus. The exam lasts 210 minutes and was first administered in 2013. It is held once a year, and the student’s score is valid for one year after the results are published. To take the exam, you must have an MBBS degree as defined by the Indian Medical Council Act.

 

There are currently 114 medical colleges and institutes (both government and private) to which you can gain admission through the NEET-PG examination.

 

Criteria for Eligibility

 

Any student pursuing an academic career in India holds a Bachelor of Medicine, Bachelor of Surgery (MBBS) degree (if the degree has not yet been awarded, a provisional pass certificate is required) according to the Indian Act of Medical Council can apply for the exam.

 

A valid Indian or State Medical Council-authorised MBBS registration certificate is also required. Only candidates who have completed a minimum of one year of internship are eligible to apply for the same Examination. For candidates who have not yet finished their training, proof of an upcoming internship program that is nearing completion will suffice.

 

If a candidate has a bachelor’s degree from a foreign medical college, he or she must take the Medical Council of India Screening Test / Foreign Medical Graduate Examination. Only after passing this exam will the student be eligible to take the Entrance Exam for the same.

 

There are two additional primary requirements for students who have graduated from Foreign Medical Colleges in order to apply for PG of NEET. To begin, the candidate must register with the Medical Council of India (Central or State) and complete a full year of internship.

 

Eligibility for NEET PG Counseling

 

MCC will establish a specific cut-off for the year. Candidates who achieve the qualifying cut-off marks set by them will be eligible to attend the NEET Counselling. Though the changes regarding cut-off on an annual basis, it remains close to 275-320 for general candidates and around 250-300 for reserved quota candidates.

 

Procedure for NEET PG Counseling

 

The entire counselling process takes place online. It goes through the following steps:

 

Registration for NEET

 

Candidates who wish to enrol for the NEET PG Counseling process must first register on the MCC’s official website and will be required to register using their official phone number/ office phone number and a valid email address.

Candidates will be given login credentials, which they must use later to complete the registration application form and upload all academic information. Candidates must pay a one-time counselling fee via Net banking after completing the registration application (online payment). The fee is usually divided into two parts: refundable and non-refundable.

 

The counselling fees for a candidate’s deemed universities are higher than the counselling fees for the AQI or Central Universities. More information is available on the website.

 

Selection Filling

 

Following registration, candidates must select their preferred colleges in order of preference. There will already be a list of colleges; you must choose which ones you want and arrange them in the order you prefer. After you’ve finished filling out the choices, save a copy of the list for future reference.

 

 Seat Allocation

 

Following that, the council will undergo the first round of seat allocation. If the candidate is offered a seat at their preferred institute, they may continue with the admission process; otherwise, the candidate may choose a free exit. Following that, MCI begins enrollment for the second round of counselling. In the second round of registration, candidates can create a new preference list in the same way they did in the first. The prior preference list will be considered void for candidates who chose a free exit after the first round.

 

Documents required for the process are the following:

 

  1. Admit Card
  2. Rank Card
  3. Marksheet Of Class X
  4. MBBS Degree Certificate
  5. MBBS Marksheet
  6. Certificate of EWS
  7. Caste certificate
  8. Registration Certificate issued by MCI/SMC
  9. Internship Completion Certificate
  10. Any disability certificate
  11. A valid photo id proof like a Voter id card/ pan card/ Aadhar card/ Passport/ Driving License

 

Process of Document Verification

If the candidate chooses admission, he or she must be available at the respective institute on a specific day for document verification, as announced by the MCI. The personnel of the assigned institutes will verify the documents on this day. Candidates must bring the original documents and self-attested photocopies of the required documents.

 

Seat Allocation Results

Typically, the total number of available seats is divided in half. This division applies to MD, MS, and Diploma programs. One-half of the seats are reserved for Central Government institutes (with a 50% quota on a pan-India basis), while the other half is reserved for state medical council institutes. A centralized counselling process, similar to the NEET UG exam, ensures seat allocation. The merit list is compiled using Score. Reservations are available for the SC, ST, OBC, PWD, and Economically Weaker Section (EWS). There are no reservations in Armed Forces Medical Service Institutions.

We assist you in selecting the best career options by providing you with a personalized report that includes information about your competitive exam scores. We also offer one-on-one sessions in which our expert counsellors assist you in making informed decisions. We will assist you in obtaining admission to the appropriate university.

posts.content:
MD/MS in India is one of the most popular career options for students interested in pursuing a Post-Graduation Medical course in INDIA. MD stands for Doctor of Medicine, and it entails three years of clinical education in the field of medicine while pursuing an MD. Students receive specialized training to treat patients/diseases using non-surgical procedures, i.e. only medicines.

MS stands for master of surgery, and it entails three years of clinical training in the field of surgery. MS students receive speciality training to treat patients/diseases using various surgical procedures.

 

INDIA MD/MS ADMISSION

 

To be admitted to MD/MS programs in INDIA, candidates must pass the NEET-PG entrance exam, which is administered by NBE each year. To apply for NEET-PG, candidates must have stable or provisional enrollment with MCI and have completed an MBBS degree from an MCI-recognized medical college/institute with a one-year mandatory internship. After passing the NEET-PG entrance exam, students must go through NEET-PG counselling at the Central and State levels.

MCC (Medical Counseling Committee) provides NEET-PG counselling on behalf of DGHS (Director General Health Secretary). Counseling for the All India Quota is done by the MCC.

  • With 100% of seats available at central universities such as AMU and BHU,
  • With AFMC, DU (Delhi universities), and ESIC hospitals all full,
  • With 100% of seats in prestigious private universities.

 

Process of applying for MD MS in India: 

Candidates must have passed the NEET -PG (National Eligibility Cumulative Entrance Test) for Medical Postgraduate Courses (MD/MS/PG -Diploma). NBE administers the NEET-PG exam online throughout India.

 

Concerning the NBE (National Board of Examinations):

The Government of India established the NBE in 1975 and provides quality education in modern medicine. The primary goal of the NBE is to conduct Postgraduate Medical Examinations across India. It is a completely online mode for the NBE exams. In India, NBE is overseen by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. According to recent changes in medical entrance exams, NBE is now conducting a single entrance exam for admissions to MD/MS/DNB programmes throughout the country.

posts.title: Why is NEET essential for Indian students interested in studying medicine?
posts.content:
If you’re wondering if NEET is essential to fulfilling your ambition of becoming a doctor, the answer is yes! NEET is required for Indian students who want to pursue a medical career in India or abroad. It makes it easy for Indian students who want to practice medicine in India after completing an MBBS or an equivalent course abroad to do so. If you want to learn more about the NEET, including the NEET requirements for an MBBS degree, we recommend that you read this blog to the end.

 

What exactly is NEET?

 

The National Eligibility Cum Admission Test (NEET) is a standardized entrance exam for Indian students interested in studying medicine in India and abroad. The National Testing Agency (NTA) administers the test in pen and paper format every year as a common entrance examination for admission to medical universities/colleges in India. Hindi, English, Assamese, Bengali, Gujarati, Marathi, Odia, Kannada, Malayalam, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu, and Urdu are the 13 languages used in the NEET.

 

Is the NEET exam required for the MBBS program?

 

Indian students seeking admission to pursue MBBS or any comparable program can easily gain admission to the Leading Medical Universities using their NEET scores. NMC/the former MCI supplies NEET-certified applicants with the registration number necessary for admission to medical courses.

 

Students must score highly in NEET in order to get admitted to a reputed medical university abroad for an MBBS degree. For MBBS admission, each university has its unique set of norms and regulations. Some universities in other countries hold their admission exams, while others do not. However, for Indian students to pursue medicine overseas, they must pass the NEET.

 

Who is eligible to apply for NEET?

 

Medical students who have completed their 10+2 with Physics, Chemistry, and Biology. Students must be 17 years old at the time of enrollment or will reach that age on or before December 31st of the year of enrollment to the first semester of the Undergraduate Medical Course. The NMC’s fourth meeting held on October 21, 2021, stated that there is no age restriction for applying for NEET.

 

Citizens or candidates from the following countries are eligible to apply for NEET:

  • Indian citizens
  • Non-Residents Indians (NRIs)
  • Indian Overseas Citizen (OCI)
  • Individuals of Indian Origin (PIO)
  • Nationals of Other Countries

 

What is the significance of NEET for Indian students?

 

NEET is a standardized entrance exam for Indian students interested in studying medicine. It is an exam designed to assess a student’s fundamental understanding of the subject in which they wish to work. Medical Universities Abroad determines a student’s capability to succeed in their MBBS journey based on their NEET score.

 

NEET gives all students who wish to pursue medicine an equal opportunity. It relieves students of the strain of studying for several tests and allows them to concentrate just on one exam in order to gain admission to the Leading Medical Institution for an MBBS degree.

 

NEET permits Indian students to study medicine at any university that has been recognized by the NMC. It allows students to pursue their ambition of becoming physicians at a low cost. Qualifying for NEET not only enables students into their preferred institution but also holds the key to their future.

 

When a student qualifies for NEET, the NMC issues a registration number. This enables students to sit for the Foreign Medical Graduates Examination (FMGE), a licensure examination administered by the National Board of Examinations for graduate medical students seeking to practice medicine in India after receiving their MBBS degree from one of the world’s top medical universities.

posts.title: MBBS in India versus MBBS Abroad for Indian Students
posts.content:
Medicine is one of the most difficult professions to enter. Admissions to MBBS programs in India or abroad place medical students in a variety of challenging conditions. The availability of professional doctors in India is quite low, resulting in stiff rivalry among medical hopefuls. As a result, under this circumstance, pursuing an MBBS abroad is becoming a viable choice. 

 

Seeking admission to study MBBS today needs an Indian student to pass the NEET. The National Eligibility and Admission Test (NEET) is the only entrance test for Indian students interested in studying medicine in India or abroad. If a student does not pass NEET, they must either drop out or pursue medicine at universities that enable them to study medicine while studying for NEET. 

Many Indian students who have been denied admission to a government medical college in India want to study MBBS abroad. The majority of students place a premium on the price as well as the prestige of the medical degree abroad. 

 

Here are a few of the most prevalent reasons why Indian medical students are perplexed while deciding whether to study MBBS abroad or in India.

 

  1. Cost-effectiveness 

Pursuing MBBS in India may be more expensive than studying MBBS elsewhere. In India, the average tuition expense for MBBS varies from INR 20 Lakhs to over INR 1 Cr. Tuition prices for MBBS Abroad might range from INR 50 Lakhs to INR 60 Lakhs for Indian students. As a result, studying MBBS abroad at Leading Medical Universities is more financially viable for Indian students. 

 

  1. Education 

Both Indian and foreign medical universities have diverse curricular systems and teaching approaches. Medical universities place an emphasis on giving students with hands-on learning opportunities to help them develop their knowledge and abilities. Medical Universities overseas, on the other hand, provide opportunities such as global experience and more.

 

  1. Eligibility Requirements 

NEET scores and rankings are used to determine admission to medical schools in India. While NEET scores are necessary for admission to medical colleges abroad, students just need to pass the entrance examination; no ranking is required. Furthermore, students must meet the minimum qualifying standards to apply for the MBBS program. 

 

At the time of entrance, the student must have reached the age of 17 years. 

The student must have finished their 12th grade through CBSE or any recognized board/state board. 

Students must have at least 50% in topics such as physics, chemistry, and biology.

 

  1. Language 

English is the most widely used language in India and many other nations across the world. There will be no linguistic barrier for Indian students studying medicine in India or abroad. However, mastering both the native and English languages may give students a wide range of opportunities for professional advancement. 

 

  1. Recognition 

Foreign Medical Universities provide MBBS degrees that are highly regarded by the world’s medical councils. The National Medical Commission has authorized many medical universities (NMC). These medical council recognitions allow Indian students to practice medicine in any country across the world. 

 

Conclusion! 

Although many Indian students choose to study MBBS in India, the restricted number of places at government medical institutions and the excessive prices imposed by private medical universities have left Indian medical aspirants with little alternative except to study medicine abroad.

After considering the above factors, it is possible to conclude that studying MBBS abroad is beneficial for Indian students. The course structure and educational quality are comparable in India and several other nations. Medical students looking for an excellent education might choose MBBS Abroad at a low cost.

posts.content:
MBBS Abroad is just as legitimate as MBBS in India. Many Indians have chosen to study medicine overseas for a variety of reasons over the years. One of the primary causes is the scarcity of medical seats at India’s government medical colleges. This makes it more difficult for Indian students to obtain a place for their medical studies in India, forcing them to study medicine overseas. 

 

Medical study overseas is regarded as one of the most desirable alternatives for Indian students. Aside from the low tuition, students have several opportunities to explore and gain experience in order to become good physicians.

 

MBBS Abroad Program Duration 

 

The length of MBBS Abroad varies by country. Some nations provide 5.5 or 6 years of medical school. 

 

The Advantages of Pursuing MBBS Abroad 

 

Some of the key advantages of studying MBBS abroad include: 

 

Reasonable Fee 

MBBS Abroad costs between 15 and 25 lakhs. Medical universities abroad are popular among Indian students who want to study medicine at a low cost. 

 

Excellent infrastructure 

Universities abroad are well equipped with cutting-edge technology that is utilized for both practical and classroom instruction. To keep the institution up to date in terms of offering medical education to students, contemporary infrastructure is being developed to keep up with the current medical sector need.

 

International acclaim 

Some medical universities in other countries are world-renowned. They are also authorized by India’s National Medical Commission. As a result, graduates with foreign medical education can practise medicine in India following FMGE. 

 

Additional MBBS seats 

More places for medical study are available in medical universities overseas. As a result, more Indian students are studying overseas. 

 

The greatest return on investment

Are you set to finish your MBBS from overseas and debating the specialization to pursue in your post-graduation? This perplexity takes over most MBBS grads’ thoughts, and they brainstorm on the matter. Whatever medical sector you select, new doors of opportunity open up for medical students after completing their MBBS overseas, allowing them to contribute to the medical industry meaningfully.

 

It goes without saying that obtaining a foreign MBBS degree will benefit your medical career. Nonetheless, a post-graduate degree in your chosen field will surely help your professional career in the future. So, carefully considering post-graduate specialization after MBBS from overseas is essential if you want to accomplish your long-held ambition of being a successful doctor.

 

Best Specializations After MBBS in Abroad

 

To be more specific, graduates with an MBBS degree and one year of internship can pursue post-graduate medical courses lasting 2-3 years, such as:

 

Specializations in Medicine (MD) Following MBBS Abroad

 

  1. Pathology Doctor of Medicine (MD): It is a three-year postgraduate medical school in medicine and illness diagnostics that teaches histology, morbid anatomy, haematology, and cytology. The Doctor of Medicine in Pathology degree provides in-depth information to cope with diagnostic issues, examinations, and interpretations in clinical pathology, microbiology, transfusion medicine, and other related fields. An MBBS graduate who wishes to pursue post-graduate studies as an M.D. in Pathology must have graduated at least 50% from an MCI-recognized medical university overseas.

 

  1. Doctor of Medicine (MD) in General Medicine: This three-year postgraduate medical program aims to produce physicians with the necessary abilities and expertise to diagnose diseases cost-effectively apply for this PG program after MBBS, candidates must have finished MBBS from a recognized university with at least 50% and a one-year mandatory internship.

 

  1. Doctor of Medicine (MD) in Pediatrics: Pediatricians are doctors who specialize in the medical treatment of children. It is a three-year post-graduate medical program that requires an MBBS degree from a recognized university as well and year a required internship following graduation.

 

  1. Doctor of Medicine (MD) in Microbiology: Microbiologists are MBBS graduates with a postgraduate degree in microbiology. This three-year medical program teaches students microbiology to reduce the spread of infectious illnesses in communities. The curriculum of the program includes theoretical and practical expertise in virology, bacteriology, immunology, parasitology, and mycology. Any MBBS graduate who applies for this program must have an MBBS degree from a recognized university and one year of the internship experience.

 

  1. Anatomy Doctor of Medicine (MD): Anatomy is the study of a person, and the doctor who studies it is known as an anatomist. M.D. in Anatomy is a three-year post-graduate degree that provides a broad knowledge of the complete human body shape to the molecular levant as a detailed comprehension of its functioning. Candidates who wish to pursue an M.D. in Anatomy after completing their MBBS from an MCI-recognized university must complete a one-year mandatory internship after their MBBS.

 

  1. Doctor of Medicine (MD) in Cardiology: Cardiology is the study of the heart in depth. Any MBBS graduate who completes this three-year post-graduate program will be able to identify and treat heart-related difficulties in their patients, such as coronary heart disease, congenital heart defects, electrophysiology, and valvular heart illnesses. This post-graduate program is open to any applicant having an MBBS degree from an MCI-recognized university plus a year of internship.

 

  1. Radiology Doctor of Medicine (MD): Radiology covers radiation diagnostics and therapy. This 3-year post-graduate medical education has developed as one of the most popular specialities following MBBS, comprising MRIs, X-rays, ultrasounds, and Computed Tomography (CT) scans. It teaches students how to perform and evaluate a variety of diagnostic imaging investigations. Candidates must have an MBBS degree to apply; furthermore, practitioners with 10+ years of clinical experience can apply for this post-graduate medical program.

 

Master of Surgery (MS) Specializations Following an Abroad MBBS

 

  1. Master of Surgery (MS) in Pediatric Surgery: This two-year postgraduate program prepares candidates to conduct surgery on young patients such as fetuses, newborns, children, adolescents, and teenagers. It also provides significant training in pediatric subspecialties such as rheumatology, pulmonary medicine, gastrointestinal, and endocrinology. To apply for this course, you must have an MBBS degree with at least a 55% graduation rate, a one-year required internship, and, in some situations, 12 months of professional experience.

 

  1. Master of Surgery (MS) in Cardiac Surgery: An M.S. in cardiac surgery is a two-year post-graduate medical degree that focuses on the surgical treatment of disorders affecting the organs of the thorax, heart, and lungs. The course focuses on providing candidates for cardiac surgery with complete training. The program focuses on building the necessary abilities in candidates for secondary and tertiary level cardiac surgical practice. Candidates must have a strong background in fundamental and applied medical sciences, cardiac critical care, cardiac surgical care, emergency departments, and other surgical fields.

Gross anatomy, orbital and ocular anatomy, ocular physiology, histology, biochemistry, microbiology, and immunology are all covered in this course. This course provides chances for ophthalmologic research in clinical surgery, such as utilizing an operating microscope, fine microsurgery, vitreoretinal surgery, or intraocular eye surgery.

 

  1. Obstetrics and Gynecology Master of Surgery (MS): This two-year postgraduate degree program focuses on female reproductive organs whether they are pregnant or not. Candidates who want to do this course must have a minimum of 50% in their MBBS.

posts.title: NMC Regulations for Transfer of Indian Students Pursuing MBBS Abroad
posts.content:
Because of the increased rivalry in the medical industry in India, many Indian students are looking for MBBS possibilities abroad. Every year, hundreds of Indian medical students study MBBS at overseas medical universities/institutions. However, many Indian students studying in medical universities in Ukraine and other foreign countries are now pursuing university admission to Indian medical colleges to finish their medical degrees. The National Medical Commission, on the other hand, has dashed the aspirations of foreign returning Indian students by rejecting their applications. This is now the only option for such Indian students.

The NMC has released recommendations in response to a series of commonly asked concerns about university transfer for Indian students pursuing MBBS in international institutions from Ukraine and other countries.

Q1. Which pupils are covered by the Screening Test Regulations, 2002?

Screening Test Regulations, 2002 apply to Indian students attending overseas medical colleges whose sessions began before November 18, 2021.

Q2. Which students are affected by the Foreign Medical Graduate Licentiate Regulations 2021?

Overseas Medical Graduate Licentiate Regulations 2021 apply to Indian students attending foreign medical schools whose sessions began after November 18, 2021.

Q3. Is the date of the admission letter/invitation letter/offer letter taken into account when determining the application of the FMGL Regulations 2021?

No.

Q4. Does NMC Public Notice No. NMC/20659

NMC/20659 28 Jul (Legal)/2022/UGMEB/ dated The NMC Public Notice No. y 2022 applies to last year’s Indian undergraduate medical students who left their medical higher education institutions abroad, returned to India due to the Ukraine war, covid-19, etc., completed their medical education, and were granted a (Legal)/2022/UGMEB/, issued July 28, 2022, apply? degree in medicine by their respective universities on or before 30th June 2022.

Q5. How long does the Compulsory Rotatory Medical Internship last for Indian students pursuing MBBS at international universities?

For Indian students studying MBBS at foreign universities, the compulsory rotatory medical internship lasts two years, with one year of internship compensating for the missing medical experience at their foreign university and the other year preparing them to practice medicine according to Indian standards.

Q6: Do Indian medical students from foreign medical colleges who qualify for the FMGE have to complete a two-year rotatory medical internship?

Yes.

Q7. Is there any relief for Indian medical graduates who passed their MBBS in July 2021?

There would be no relief for Indian medical graduates who received their MBBS degree in July 2021. It is only provided to foreign medical graduates who finished their MBBS on or before June 30, 2022, according to a Supreme Court of India judgment.

Q8. Can Indian students studying in Ukraine transfer to another university?

The Screening Test Regulation, 2002 applies to every Indian medical student attending a Ukrainian university whose classes begin on or before November 18, 2021. As long as the other conditions of the Regulations are met, such students are not restricted from transferring to any university.

However, the FMGL Regulations 2021 apply to Indian students admitted to Ukrainian institutions after November 18, 2021, and they compel them to authenticate their undergraduate courses within Regulation 4 of the FMGL Regulations 2021. They must complete all of their medical education, training, apprenticeships, and clerkships in the same medical facility.

Q9. Can Indian students go from a six-year to a five-year MBBS program?

Any Indian student registered in a foreign medical institution that is subject to the Screening Test Regulations, 2002 may move from a 6-year MBBS program to a 5-year MBBS program.

Q10. Is a letter of recommendation from NMC necessary to move between abroad medical universities?

No, a letter of authorization from the National Medical Commission is not necessary to transfer between foreign medical universities because these schools are not within the jurisdiction of the NMC.

Q11: What should Indian students consider before enrolling at abroad medical schools?

The FMGL Regulations 2021 will apply to all medical students in India who begin their education after November 18, 2021. They must finish their whole clinical training, training, internship, and externship at the same foreign medical institution or university. there is no chance of moving to another university in another country for medical education or training.

Q12 What regulations apply to freshmen accepted to foreign medical colleges under the FMGL Regulations, 2021?

The following are the FMGL Regulations, 2021 conditions regulating Indian students’ future admission to abroad medical universities:

Medical undergraduate programs must run for at least 54 months or 4.5 years.

There is a minimum 12-month medical internship available at the same foreign medical university or institution.

The teaching language is English.

Schedule-1 of the FMGL Regulations, 2021 covers the necessary subjects.

The regulatory authority that issues the medical license in the country where the medical degree is conferred is equal to the regulatory body that issues the license in the other nation.

Q13: Has the NMC authorized the Ukraine mobility program?

The NMC does not support Ukraine’s mobility initiative.

(We would like to notify students that various mobility programs are now in operation in Georgia and Ukraine, and NMC has emphasized that no such Mobility Programs for MBBS are legitimate.) As a result, if you are a Ukrainian student, kindly do not apply for migration programs in Georgia or Ukraine).

Q14. Can Indian MBBS students from Ukraine study in Indian medical schools?

Ukraine-returned Indian MBBS students are not permitted to attend Indian medical schools.

Q15. Is there a list of international medical universities that the NMC has approved?

No, the NMC does not provide such a list since such medical institutes are not approved or recognized by the NMC for the granting of any medical certification.

Q16. Which document is approved as legitimate by NMC for Indian MBBS graduates from abroad colleges to take the next exam?

The National Medical Commission is reviewing the draught for the next test, which will be made public once finished.

Final Thoughts

Following multiple rounds of conjecture over the admittance of Ukraine-returned Indian medical students or Indian medical graduates to Indian medical institutions, the NMC has now put all of them to rest by publishing this announcement. At the very least, they may now explore choices in other countries, allowing them to restart their medical education and get a real medical degree, paving the way for a successful medical career.

Students in their first year of MBBS can apply for fresh admissions to overseas medical colleges, and students in future years can continue their MBBS at top medical universities or institutes abroad.

A Comprehensive Guide for Indian Medical Aspirants to MBBS in India

Medical education in India is a major topic among debaters, owing to the country’s ever-increasing severe rivalry in the medical field. Every year, millions of Indian students take medical entrance exams in order to get admission to India’s top medical schools. Unfortunately, only a tiny number of medical students qualify for such tests.

With the NEET UG test just a few days ago and the results about to be revealed, science students have expedited their quest for various medical institutions in India. Although their NEET score will have a big influence on their admissions, students are already interested in learning about the many medical colleges, including their admission procedure, pricing structures, eligibility requirements, and more. When it comes to applying for admission to the finest medical institutions in the country, every second matters, as thousands of NEET-qualified candidates will be submitting applications. So, speeding up the admission procedure is the key to getting into your preferred medical institutions in India.

MBBS Program in India

Medical school is the most sought-after profession among Indian students. The bulk of medical applicants wants to pursue MBBS in India from top medical schools and institutes in order to have a great medical future ahead of them.

What Exactly is MBBS

MBBS, or Bachelor of Medicine, Bachelor of Surgery, is a five-and-a-half-year undergraduate degree program in medicine available to medical students who have passed the NEET.

CriteriaDetails
Who is eligible to apply?Students who have studied Physics, Chemistry, Biology, and English in their 12th grade
are eligible to apply for the MBBS program. The MBBS degree is primarily intended for
students who wish to become physicians.
What is the time frame?In India, the MBBS program lasts 5.5 years, including 4.5 years of academic study
and 1 year of compulsory rotatory internship.

What Are The MBBS Eligibility Requirements in India

Candidates who wish to pursue a bachelor’s degree in medicine and a bachelor’s degree in surgery must meet the following requirements in order to be admitted to the MBBS program in India:

  1. To take the NEET exam, you must be at least 17 years old.
  2. Attained at least 50% in the 12th grade.
  3. The NEET test must be passed by all candidates.
  4. Accomplished the 12th grade with honours in physics, chemistry, and biology.
  5. In India, the maximum age for applying to the MBBS course is 25 years.

Specializations in MBBS

Through their MBBS degree programs, Indian medical institutes strive to deliver cutting-edge, growth-oriented education. With the increased need for medical experts in the market, the opportunities for medical students to do MBBS courses in India are limitless. Students in MBBS courses can pick their desired speciality depending on their interests and professional ambitions.

MBBS SpecializationDescription
OphthalmologyOphthalmology is a branch of medicine that deals with the treatment of eye abnormalities and illnesses.
General MedicineGeneral medicine is the study of the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of adult illnesses.
GastroenterologyThe MBBS degree program tackles problems of the oesophagus, small bowel, stomach, liver, colon, pancreas, gallbladder, and bile ducts, as well as the thyroid gland on occasion.
OrthopaedicsOrthopaedics is the study of the treatment of illnesses in the skeletal system.
PaediatricsPaediatrics is a branch of medicine that deals with the care of newborns and children.
Obstetrics and GynecologyThis medical field assists in the diagnosis and treatment of illnesses and problems in the female reproductive system.
ENT (Ear, Nose, and Throat)This specialization focuses on the treatment of ear, nose, and throat problems.
AnaesthesiologyThis specialization involves relieving patients’ pain and providing care before, during, and after surgery.
PsychiatryPsychiatry is the study and treatment of mental illnesses.
DermatologyThis specialization focuses on diagnosing and treating skin disorders.

Medical Admission Exams in India

A strong NEET score is required to gain admission to a good and top medical institution in India to pursue MBBs. Previously, in India, three medical entrance tests determined the fate of prospective medical students:

AIIMS (All India Institute of Medical Science) entrance exam NEET (National Eligibility Entrance Test) JIPMER (Jawaharlal Institute of PG Medical Education & Research)

However, starting in 2022, the NEET test became the primary medical entrance exam in India, and AIIMS and JIPMER were included in the NEET exam beginning in session 2021. To get admission to premier medical colleges and institutes in India, like JIPMER and AIIMS, medical students must now just take the NEET test.

NEET (National Eligibility Entrance Test)

Indian students who want to be recognized and successful medical professionals in India or abroad must pass the NEET test. The higher the NEET score, the higher the chances of getting into the top medical colleges.

The Bottom Line

Indian students always seek to obtain a place in Indian medical institutions and reserve MBBS overseas as a last resort if they are unable to gain a seat in India. The complete study will provide MBBS hopefuls with a better idea of available seats and their alternatives in India.
